major_risks.risk: Demand for the company's products is cyclical and highly sensitive to global and regional economic conditions, commodity prices, infrastructure spending and construction and housing activity.

Tariffs and other trade-policy changes can raise costs and reduce demand. The report cites higher tariffs as the main driver of unfavorable manufacturing costs in 2025 and expects about $2.6 billion of tariff impact in 2026.
major_risks.source: Item 1A, 'International trade policies may impact demand for our products and our competitive position' (p. 18); Item 7 MD&A (p. 29, 33)

major_risks.risk: The Financial Products segment (Cat Financial) depends on access to capital markets and credit ratings and is exposed to customer credit losses and interest-rate changes, and restrictive debt covenants could limit flexibility.

limits: Operating income is the line labeled 'Operating profit' in Statement 1, which includes Financial Products' interest expense and other operating items, so it is not a pure industrial operating margin.

Capex uses the published line 'Capital expenditures – excluding equipment leased to others' (2,821). Including equipment leased to others (1,465, mostly Cat Financial), free cash flow would be lower. Choose the basis you prefer.

Total financial debt (43,330) and net debt (33,350) are consolidated and include about 32.6 billion of Financial Products debt. MP&E-only debt is 10,713 (35 + 10,678) against MP&E cash of 9,333, which the analyst may prefer.
The Rail division moves from Power & Energy to Resource Industries. A Form 8-K in March 2026 will recast the segments, so segment figures here are as reported for 2025 (p. 29).
The three major risks are my selection from Item 1A. The company does not rank its risks, and the tariff risk draws on both Item 1A and Item 7.
The 2026 guidance is mostly qualitative and expressed as growth rates and amounts, with no EPS or profit target.
